key_insight: Bobbin Tool Friction Stir Welding enabled direct bonding of aluminum face sheets to an aluminum foam core without adhesives or brazing materials.
engineering_relevance: The process offers a potential joining route for lightweight sandwich panels used in transportation, aerospace, and military structures.
method: Fabricate aluminum/aluminum foam/aluminum sandwich joints using BT-FSW.
Use selected welding conditions of 1250 rpm rotation and 12 mm/min traverse speed.
Evaluate compression, three-point bending, and interfacial shear responses.
evidence_signal: The welded sample reached 99.1 MPa compressive stress at 0.3135 strain, 7250.8 N maximum bending load, and 2104 N maximum interfacial shear load.
watch_item: The abstract does not report repeatability, fatigue performance, or comparisons with adhesive or brazed joints, limiting conclusions about service readiness.
paper_title: Evaluation of the mechanical behavior of aluminum/aluminum foam/aluminum sandwich panels fabricated by Bobbin Tool Friction Stir Welding
